anatomy.name: Agent Core (model routing + reasoning)
anatomy.role: Cognitive engine: interprets input, selects one of the 20 workflow patterns, decides actions.
anatomy.implementation: AgentCore.route_and_reason(prompt, context) behind a provider-agnostic LLM gateway.
anatomy.governance: Achievement is attested here, not inferred. The Top Admin replicates only on attestation + a necessity decision.

anatomy.name: Orchestration & workflow execution
anatomy.role: Control flow: executes the chosen workflow pattern and manages state.
anatomy.implementation: WorkflowEngine.run(workflow, input, context, llm, tools) over a DAG/state machine of stage nodes.
anatomy.governance: Stages run sequentially; a closed gate stops the DAG and downstream stages are skipped, never faked.

anatomy.name: Memory & knowledge
anatomy.role: Context and persistence: short-term conversation history and long-term retrieval.
anatomy.governance: Each spawned compartment keeps an isolated store; sharing only via permissioned handoffs.

anatomy.name: Tools & actions
anatomy.implementation: ToolRegistry of callables with JSON schemas (function calling, workflow 12).
anatomy.governance: Only agents explicitly authorized for the compartment may trigger high-stakes rails.

anatomy.name: Interfaces & triggers
anatomy.implementation: InterfaceAdapter layer: cron, webhook, chat, and voice adapters call the workflow engine.
anatomy.governance: Triggers are recorded as evidence; they never count as achievement on their own.

anatomy.name: Observability & evaluation
anatomy.role: Feedback loop: trace actions, evaluate performance, catch errors.
anatomy.implementation: Tracer logs every state transition; an Evaluator node checks a rubric before the workflow proceeds.
anatomy.governance: The evaluator produces the achievement attestation the engine consumes; it is an input, not a self-verdict.

anatomy.name: Deployment & scaling
anatomy.role: Infrastructure that keeps agents running and spawns new ones.
anatomy.implementation: Per-component images (Rust/CMake/Qt baked in) and a deploy orchestrator for worker pools.
anatomy.governance: Spawning is capped and fail-closed; a failed spawn halts the cascade instead of skipping ahead.

gaps.gap: There is no in-process model gateway. Model work belongs to the freellmapi/grok-jev-router components, and this engine attests reasoning rather than performing it.
Single-process orchestration; no durable execution across restarts beyond run replay.
MCP is implemented (one shared server); A2A is not. Agent-to-agent handoff is mediated by the router and admin, not a peer protocol.
No embedding index or vector store. Retrieval is metadata and keyword lookup over local stores, so similarity search is designed but not implemented.
No container orchestrator. Replication is registry-level (an agent record plus a reporting edge), not a new isolated process.
Single local dashboard and JSON API; no public or multi-tenant surface.
No peer agent-to-agent protocol, discovery, or capability negotiation. Handoffs are hierarchical, which is deliberate, but it is not A2A.
No ontology or knowledge graph store; relationships are code-level conventions.
No business glossary data product; the glossary above is curated, not queryable.
No vector embeddings, so 'similar meaning' is lexical today.

replication.assignment: compartment-agnostic: any workflow may staff any compartment
replication.decision: necessity is decided per run by decide_compartments (hints, goal evidence, signals); default threshold 2.0
replication.rule: achievement attestation -> necessity decision -> selected compartments only, in canonical order
fail_closed: closed stage gate -> DAG stops, downstream stages skipped
no compartment above threshold -> no cascade
first failed spawn -> cascade halts; remaining compartments skipped
replication.decider_seam: pass a custom decider (e.g. LLM/agent-backed) to decide_compartments; output is normalized and validated
